title: Does Homogeneity Defeat Majority-Vote Self-Consistency on Safety Questions?

original_idea.body:
# Does Homogeneity Defeat Majority-Vote Self-Consistency on Safety Questions?

**Problem:** Self-consistency is a popular reliability boost proposed across models for safety. But if models share blind spots, the majority can be confidently wrong together.

**Direction:** On a safety/factual QA set with ground truth, build cross-model ensembles and measure when majority vote fails because models err identically. Compare high-homogeneity vs low-homogeneity ensembles. Quantify how much diversity is needed before voting helps.

**Why it matters:** Directly tests whether the 'ensemble for safety' intuition survives monoculture - and gives a recipe (pick dissimilar models).

**Relevant context:** Great Models Think Alike (arXiv:2502.04313); Correlated Errors (arXiv:2506.07962).
